history.preflop: BTN opens 5bb, BB 3-bets to 18bb, BTN calls

villain.desc: Plays the equilibrium strategy. The 2200 anchor of the ladder.
villain.name: GTO

history.preflop: BTN opens 5bb, BB 3-bets to 18bb, BTN calls

villain.desc:
Loose-passive calling station. Calls far too much, rarely raises, almost never bluffs, and
checks a lot of hands he should bet. When he does bet, he has it.
The most common profitable opponent at $1/$2.
villain.name: Station
notes: never folds a pair to a normal bet
calls off top pair against an overbet or shove
but usually lets go of weaker pairs when the bet is huge
floats too much with nothing, but does give up eventually
calls instead of raising, except with the nuts
bets smaller than he should with value

history.preflop: BTN opens 5bb, BB 3-bets to 18bb, BTN calls

villain.desc:
Tight-passive. Folds too much to pressure, only raises the nuts, and his big bets and raises
are almost never bluffs. Respect his aggression, attack his checks.
villain.name: Nit
notes: folds too much when he isn't strong

history.preflop: BTN opens 5bb, BB 3-bets to 18bb, BTN calls

villain.desc:
Loose-aggressive to a fault. Bets and raises far too often, especially with air and draws,
and folds too little. Call him down lighter; let him bluff.
villain.name: Maniac

history.preflop: BTN opens 5bb, BB 3-bets to 18bb, BTN calls

villain.desc:
The recreational player who is there to gamble. Calls almost anything, raises every draw,
and sizes his bets by hand strength (big = strong, small = not).
villain.name: Whale
notes: size tell: big bet = big hand
size tell: small bet = weak or drawing
